decisions.reason: Healthcare and hospitality recruitment remains far from the firm's maritime knowledge base and digital-maritime strategy, so absorptive capacity is weak and management would now reallocate resources to closer maritime businesses.
Superyacht crew recruitment is a close extension of the firm's established crewing and training capabilities, making it easy to learn from the market and improve with existing networks.
The maritime education programme builds directly on the firm's training centres and know-how, and the early expansion to six partner institutions signals promising assimilation and scaling potential.
Emissions monitoring and compliance services are tightly linked to the firm's ship-management expertise and already showed strong execution by completing all required FuelEU plans on time.
The emissions compliance dashboard fits the firm's digitalisation path and existing PAL software, so related knowledge is strong even if commercial uptake is still in an early phase.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool also builds on the firm's compliance and software capabilities, but as a newer analytical tool it carries somewhat higher adoption and monetisation uncertainty than the dashboard.
